caption: Scorecard habit at its origin: the Dec-2012 promises (4-7% revenue CAGR, mid-60s OR by 2016, >$900m cash flow before dividends) set beside 2014E delivery of 8% revenue CAGR and >$1B - the template every later CP deck reuses.

The 2014 targets for 2018 in hard numbers: $10B revenue, 58-63% operating ratio, >100% EPS growth, $1.4-1.6B annual capex, >$6B cumulative cash flow before dividends. FY2018 delivered $7,316m revenue, 61.3% OR and +71% adjusted EPS.
The 2014 plan to re-weight the book of business by 2018 - Bulk 42%→34%, Merchandise 39%→46%, Intermodal 19%→20% - on merchandise revenue CAGR of 14% and intermodal 12%.

Real estate as a monetisation program: >$1B of gross sale value in surplus land plus >$100m/yr of ancillary revenue from cell towers, fibre, advertising and leases over three to five years. The later decks hold the same land as growth capacity instead.
Capital priorities and the return ambition CP set for itself in 2014: adjusted return on capital employed from 9.8% (2012) to 12.4% (2014E) to >15% by 2018.

The Norfolk Southern bid's value case: US$1.8B of claimed value, 72% of it pre-merger operational improvement CP said it could deliver inside NS from trust approval alone - train, locomotive and workforce productivity - and only 28% from combination synergies.
source_deck: 2015-12-16 · Investor update on the Norfolk Southern proposal

caption: How management framed the 2012-2018 turnaround in retrospect: lowered cost base, streamlined assets, rebuilt team, precision railroading - the 'rebuilt the engine' phase that every subsequent deck treats as completed.

The stated shift from an operations-led to a commercially-led company: pre-2012 commercially-driven, 2012-2016 operationally-driven, 2017 and beyond 'sustainable, profitable growth' sold through per-market playbooks.
2018 capital plan: $1.6B a year for 2018-2020, split 50% basic replacement, 25% rolling stock, 5% network improvement, 5% IT, 4% PTC - with long-term management compensation tied to ROIC.

The 2018 financial principles, the highest bar CP ever set publicly: $1.6B capex, >15% adjusted ROIC, 25-30% dividend payout, ~3% annual buyback, BBB+ rating. The 2023 plan asks only for a return to double-digit ROIC.

2018-2020 financial targets stated only as directions - mid-single-digit RTM growth, continued margin improvement, double-digit EPS growth CAGR, $1.6B capex - dropping the absolute revenue and cash-flow numbers the 2014 deck had committed to.
KCS transaction terms: 2.884 CP shares plus US$90 cash per KCS share, US$300/share at announcement, a 34% premium, CP/KCS ownership 72/28, US$8.5B of committed debt, Keith Creel as CEO.
source_deck: 2021-09-16 · CP and Kansas City Southern to combine

caption: The US$1B synergy commitment and its composition: US$820m from revenue and market opportunities versus US$180m of cost and efficiency savings, within three years of closing - raised from US$600m then US$780m before announcement.
source_deck: 2021-09-16 · CP and Kansas City Southern to combine

caption: Management's answer to the charge that precision railroading starves the asset: CP train accident frequency 29% below the Class 1 average in 2013 and 69% below by 2022, with CP-standalone capital investment rising from $1,104m (2011) to $1,557m (2022).
Room to Grow 2.0 - the reframing of land from something to sell into >6,000 acres of developable capacity held across the network, with Port Arthur, Dallas and Kansas City called out.

The single largest quantitative claim in the CPKC deck history: a ~US$5B multi-year revenue opportunity pipeline built from US$1,500m industrial development and nearshoring, US$1,400m truck-to-rail, US$1,100m other self-help and US$925m rail-to-rail. No date is attached to any of it.
The truck-competitiveness proof point for Mexico: San Luis Potosí to Chicago in 3.9 days actual on MMX 180/181 against 4.0 days by truck, 5.0 days advertised and 6.8 days by interchange rail.

Synergy progress two months after taking control of KCS: US$240m of annualised actuals against ~US$950m of line of sight, stacked from MMX, Lázaro Cárdenas, temperature-controlled, auto, grain and fertilizer, industrial development and ECP.

Under the heading 'Delivered On Our Commitments', CPKC reports high single-digit core adjusted EPS growth for 2018-2022 - below the double-digit EPS CAGR the 2018 Investor Day had targeted - alongside 420bp of margin improvement and >16% adjusted ROIC.

The 2024-2028 outlook as first issued: high single-digit revenue growth, strong margin improvement, free cash conversion ~90% of core adjusted income, a return to double-digit adjusted ROIC and double-digit core adjusted EPS growth.
The 2023-2028 capital plan: $2.6-2.8B a year after $2.2B in 2022 and $2.7B in 2023E. Actual spend was $2,825m in 2024 and $3,102m in 2025, above the top of the band in both years.

The deleveraging path sold in 2023: 3.8x net debt to adjusted EBITDA in 2022, 3.0x in 2023E and a flat 2.5x from 2024 through 2028, with shareholder returns to be revisited in 2024. The 2026 decks state a 2.75x target and buybacks restarted in 2025.

The performance record management presents to justify the plan: CP market capitalisation from $18B in 2012 to $97B in June 2023, an 18% CAGR, split into a 'rebuilt the engine' phase and a 'pivot to growth' phase.

The first post-merger reset: 2023 core adjusted combined diluted EPS guidance cut to flat-to-slightly-positive versus 2022, while a Mexico Task Force lifted CPKC de México car miles per car day 31% and cut terminal dwell 14% in ten weeks.
Volume since the merger, with the coal drag separated out: cumulative Q2 RTM growth of 17% from 2023 to 2026, and 22% excluding coal.

Cash deployment in 2026: operating cash flow up 8% to $2,702m, capital additions down 2%, shareholder returns up 11% to $2,371m, with ~37% of the 5% buyback programme complete and capex heading for a ~15% cut versus 2025.

The safety reversal inside a company that says safety is foundational: YTD 2026 FRA train accident frequency up 37% to 0.93 per million train-miles and personal injuries up 11% to 0.94, while speed, weight and fuel efficiency all improved.

The revenue base the growth story sits on: 2025 freight revenue 36% bulk, 46% merchandise, 18% intermodal, and by geography 41% cross-border, 33% domestic, 26% global - with the 2025 change by commodity line beside it.
Capital spending against the plan: $2.2B (2022), $2.7B (2023), $2.8B (2024), $3.1B (2025), then $2.65B guided for 2026 against a stated $2.6-2.8B band, including an $800m Tier 4 locomotive programme.

2026 guidance: low double-digit core adjusted EPS growth on $4.61, mid-single-digit RTM growth, ~$2.65B capex - resting on a $441m pension recovery, above the $330-370m assumed in the long-term plan, and a 24.75% tax rate.
The 2024-2028 targets three years on, unchanged, with a footnote conceding that four of their macro assumptions - CAD/USD, diesel, pension recovery and tax rate - have all moved since June 2023.

Grain splits that appear nowhere in the 10-K text: Canada and the U.S. each half of grain revenue, Canadian grain 68% regulated under the maximum revenue entitlement and 32% not, U.S. grain 82% domestic-destined.
International intermodal by port: Vancouver 65%, Lázaro Cárdenas 13%, Montreal 10%, Saint John 8% - showing how small the Mexican Pacific gateway still is against the West Coast Canadian franchise.
